races.name: Truelove Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Tom Clover ridden by 3lb claimer Jack Callan, returning after 39 days; the flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a serious concern on Good To Firm ground over this trip and makes it hard to trust in a shape where the leader is never pressured.

runners_data.name: Bownder
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's hold-up performer has the most relevant form in the field — placed on similar going at this trip, including a win at 10f on Standard and second at 10f on Standard — Paddy Bradley takes over and if any hold-up horse can bridge the gap to Sansanetti it is this one on the back of that consistent placed record.

runners_data.name: Cuban Girl
runners_data.note: A natural rear-of-field racer whose best figures have come when able to produce a late burst, but shuffled into a midfield map position here because the true hold-up spots are oversubscribed; four runs on Standard and Good-to-Soft without a win, and the trip up to 1m2f is unproven, complicating her chances further.

runners_data.name: Baloo's Blues
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner back after 92 days, a lengthy absence that is immediately notable; at heart a hold-up horse placed into a midfield role by the crowded tail of this field, and while two recent placed efforts on Standard at 7-8f show ability, the step to 1m2f and the layoff are both untested variables.

runners_data.name: Sansanetti
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the pivot of the whole race — Stuart Williams's filly has won twice and placed twice from six starts on Standard at Lingfield, and Pat Cosgrave's big-race experience gives her every chance of dictating an uncontested gallop; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is technically in a slightly unusual tactical role but her record shows she thrives making the running here.

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — flagged as such in the race data; Gary & Moore's hold-up type who returned placed twice at 10f on Good would have contributed to the crowded hold-up section, but takes no further part.

races.paceDynamic: Sansanetti is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and will stride to the front unchallenged, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground over 1m2f at Lingfield. With no rival capable or willing to press her, Pat Cosgrave can dictate every yard of the race, controlling the tempo and shutting down any finishing kick from behind. The bulk of the field — Revelio, Bownder, Cuban Girl, Baloo's Blues, and Gone Rogue — are all hold-up or rear-of-field types, meaning they will be chasing a horse who dictates on her own terms. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the prominent/front-running profile: a steady, uncontested lead on fast ground at this trip is a powerful tactical advantage, and closers will need the pace to be genuinely strong enough to reel Sansanetti in, which is far from guaranteed. Note that the field contains considerably more hold-up types than can realistically be separated at the rear — Cuban Girl, Gone Rogue, and Baloo's Blues are all genuine hold-up horses shuffled into the midfield map positions, and none of them will naturally get the clean passage they need in a field running in a bunch behind a lone leader.

scenarios.body: If Sansanetti is allowed to stride clear and control a measured pace throughout, she goes wire to wire.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Sansanetti fades badly inside the final furlong and multiple hold-up horses arrive together in a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: If Sansanetti fades badly inside the final furlong and multiple hold-up horses arrive together in a blanket finish.

scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Midfield Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up pack become embroiled in traffic behind Sansanetti and the race devolves into a muddled, inconclusive finish.
scenarios.body: If the hold-up pack become embroiled in traffic behind Sansanetti and the race devolves into a muddled, inconclusive finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sansanetti's price at the off — if she shortens significantly it confirms market confidence in the uncontested lead theory and Cosgrave's ability to control from the front.

Bownder is the only hold-up horse with a directly comparable form line at this trip on similar ground; watch where Paddy Bradley positions him in the early stages — any attempt to sit closer than usual could signal a real live challenge.

With Gone Rogue a non-runner the field is reduced to five genuine starters, further thinning the traffic behind Sansanetti and removing one hold-up rival who might have forced a faster pace — this makes a slow, controlled lead even more likely.

Cuban Girl, Baloo's Blues, and Revelio are all hold-up types competing for the same real estate at the rear of the field; a scrimmage for position between them in the early stages could cost any one of them vital lengths and effectively end their race before the turn.

The Good To Firm ground reported for this 5:55 race is faster than the Standard turf surface listed — watch whether any runners are withdrawn on going grounds and whether Sansanetti's connections are content with conditions, given her winning form came on Standard.

races.name: Chris, Aleah And Ellanna Family Day Out Handicap

runners_data.name: Savvy Disko
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Standard at Lingfield last time out and goes here fresh (46 days), with the front-running berth entirely his own in a five-runner field; the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is technically running at a premium position, but in this shape that simply means he is the lone pace-setter — Good To Firm suits (1W1P in similar going) and Jack Callan's claim gives a weight advantage.|

runners_data.name: Knight Of Glory
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form over 8f on Standard at Lingfield and has course form that directly applies; the 127-day layoff is the primary concern and David Menuisier sends runners back fit after breaks, headgear notation flags a hood, and his prominent style makes him the most natural beneficiary of sitting second to Savvy Disko throughout.|

runners_data.name: Suddenly I See
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's in-form yard (6/51 in 14 days) gives significant stable confidence, and Pat Cosgrave takes the ride, but this horse's natural instinct is to race prominently — with Savvy Disko already occupying that role and Knight Of Glory likely to track, Suddenly I See will be forced to settle further back than he wants, reducing his chance of producing his best form.|

runners_data.name: Magical Merlot
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a win over 8f on Good and placed efforts, with Ed Dunlop's stable showing a win in the last fortnight (1/17); Paddy Bradley rides and the horse's true front-running instinct will be suppressed by the crowded prominent end of this field, meaning he races in an unfamiliar held-up position and must produce a better closing effort than his form suggests he possesses.|

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe partners this hold-up filly who won over 10f Good last time (LR:14d) and clearly stays well, but 1m1f at Lingfield is shorter than her winning trip and the uncontested pace set by Savvy Disko is unlikely to generate the strong gallop she needs to deliver her late challenge; trainer Ollie Sangster has two winners from 25 in 14 days showing yard form, yet the shape works against her.|

races.paceDynamic: Savvy Disko is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the gates on Good To Firm ground over 1m1f at Lingfield, setting a sustainable and uncontested tempo with no genuine rival to push the pace up early. Knight Of Glory is the one horse who can sit closest in a tracking role, with Mayaada certain to be last of the five from her hold-up style. The field contains more prominent types than the shape can accommodate — Suddenly I See and Magical Merlot are both natural prominent racers who will find Savvy Disko has taken their ground, forcing them to settle deeper than ideal. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can either lead and control from the front or track the leader in second and produce a measured late effort, with the lone pace-setter dictating terms and the hold-up horse Mayaada facing the most ground to make up from the rear on what is essentially a one-horse-sets-the-fractions scenario.

scenarios.body: If Savvy Disko jumps well, dictates a measured gallop unchallenged and sustains the tempo into the straight.

scenarios.title: Tracker Runs Down Leader

scenarios.body: If Savvy Disko's pace proves just too strong in the final two furlongs and a close tracker picks up the pieces.

scenarios.body: If both Suddenly I See and Magical Merlot settle better than expected from their unnatural midfield position and produce a strong late run.

scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a closing run for the sole hold-up horse over this trip.

watchPoints.text: Savvy Disko holds the race by the throat — watch whether he jumps sharply and immediately establishes a clear lead, because if he does the race is essentially over bar Scenario B.

Knight Of Glory's 127-day absence is the single biggest variable: watch the market and paddock closely for signs of condition, as a fit return immediately promotes him to the most dangerous rival in a tracking role.

Suddenly I See and Magical Merlot are both natural front-runners — watch whether either attempts to pressure Savvy Disko early; if they do, the pace lifts and the scenario changes entirely from controlled to contested.

Mayaada is the only true hold-up horse in the field — watch whether the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and set up a closing run, as on an easy gallop she will simply have too much ground to find at the death.

races.name: Fabric First Pass The Post Handicap

runners_data.name: Stage Show
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer in good recent form (win last time out over 1m2f Good, finishing 1st), trained by Alexandra Dunn with Pat Cosgrave booked; the step up to 1m5f from 1m2f is worth monitoring given hist distances, but Good To Firm suits and the hold-up style is well-matched to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Trooper
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old arrives on a 22-day break carrying the hood (hg:b) and with Harry Vigors claiming 5lb; a hold-up horse whose recent runs include placed efforts over 1m6f on Good, suggesting stamina is not in doubt, though soft-ground form dominates his recent history and this faster surface is a mild query.

runners_data.name: Kotari
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore yard has 2 winners from 24 over 14 days which is modest, and this seven-year-old's sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 15 comparable going runs is a significant flag; his natural running style is genuine hold-up, so although placed on the map at midfield due to field congestion at the rear, he would typically race further back than that suggests.

runners_data.name: Captain Brett
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old returns just nine days after winning over 1m4f on Good To Firm, carrying no headgear and with Stevie Donohoe up; the trainer's T14 strike rate is 1/9 and the recent winner's form is compelling, but his true running style is hold-up rather than the midfield map position implies — the redistribution reflects field shape, not any natural desire to race prominently.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's four-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and gets a free lead on Good To Firm over 1m5f; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is useful, and his sim-going record of 3 wins and 6 places from 15 comparable efforts is the strongest in the field, though the step up from 1m3f to 1m5f is a stamina question at the class level.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 1m5f handicap on Good To Firm at Lingfield, and with no genuine rival to press him early, he is likely to slot into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the outset. The four remaining runners — Stage Show, Trooper, Kotari, and Captain Brett — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Jack Langley faces zero competition for the front and can dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop across the full trip. Kotari and Captain Brett are genuine hold-up horses that have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; neither is likely to race as prominently as their mapped position suggests, and Stage Show and Trooper are equally content to track from the back. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace over a staying trip on fast ground — strongly favours a hold-up horse with a strong finish or, paradoxically, rewards the front-runner if the gallop is economical enough that Jack Langley never gets run out of it; true staying closers who can unleash a sustained run from two furlongs out are best placed, but any advantage is blunted if Jack Langley has been allowed to coast.

scenarios.body: If Jack Langley dictates an untroubled, economical pace and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in the straight.

Stage Show stepped up in trip last time and won over 1m2f; another significant distance jump to 1m5f today is worth monitoring in-running to see if Pat Cosgrave has to commit earlier than ideal.

Captain Brett runs just nine days after his win and is a hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to redistribution — watch whether Donohoe elects to track closer to the leader early, which would signal a live chance under the short-turnaround bounce risk.

Kotari's zero wins and zero places in 15 runs on similar fast ground is the starkest datapoint in the race — watch whether he travels smoothly or comes under pressure before the straight, as early distress would confirm the going is against him.
Trooper carries the hood and arrives from a soft-ground background; watch the betting market moves close to post time for any sign the Mulholland team expect the faster surface to be overcome.

races.name: Choice Training Handicap

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Strong record at five furlongs on fast ground with three wins from this configuration, trained by Adam Kirby whose stable is in reasonable nick at 1/10 over 14 days — the et headgear suggests controlled forward-going and the prominent tracking role here is squarely within this horse's comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with two wins to its name, though James Owen's stable is firing at only 10/57 over 14 days and the sim-going record on fast surfaces reads just 0W1P from three starts — it can control but converting that control into victory is a question this form string leaves open.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a consistent placing record including two seconds and a third in recent starts; the 15-day layoff is not a concern, but Kiss And Run is fully dependent on the pace being honest enough to reel in — if Rogue Bullet saunters in front, this profile is compromised.

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride for Richard Hughes who has hit 3/22 in the last fortnight — Lazzar is a true hold-up type with a strong sim-going record of 4W6P on the clock but recent form reads 830694, which is patchy, and the 18-day absence adds a small question mark about sharpness on a quick surface.

runners_data.name: Sam's Xpress
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature with four wins and seven places on Standard five-furlong tracks, but displaced to midfield on the pace map because this field cannot accommodate two prominent horses simultaneously — the 99-day layoff is the most significant red flag, and the trainer's 0/4 form over 14 days adds little confidence that the absence has been bridged well.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Bullet is the confirmed pace-setter here and, critically, faces no genuine pressure for the lead in a five-runner field — Ancient State and Sam's Xpress both carry prominent tendencies but neither is a pure tearaway, meaning Rogue Bullet can dictate at a controlled, comfortable tempo on Good To Firm ground. With the pace uncontested and the race run on a flat five furlongs, the gallop is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the finish and shortens the gap between front and back. Sam's Xpress is a genuine prominent type who has been mapped back to midfield purely because the race shape has no room for two horses in that lead-framing role — in reality, Ancient State is the more likely candidate to sit directly behind Rogue Bullet and take the prominent berth. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a late charge — Kiss And Run and Lazzar are the two best-placed profiles — but only if the pace is truly honest; if Rogue Bullet controls proceedings unchallenged at a falsely steady tempo, the prominent stalkers like Ancient State who can travel into the race and quicken at the right moment stand to benefit most.

scenarios.body: If Rogue Bullet settles beautifully and the modest five-runner field fails to generate any serious late challenge.

scenarios.body: If Sam's Xpress pushes hard to recover its natural position and forces a messy, pressured early pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sam's Xpress at the start — if Dylan Hogan pushes hard to recover its natural prominent position, it could press Rogue Bullet into an unplanned faster pace and completely alter the race shape for everyone behind.

Ancient State's weight of 138lbs is notable at the top of the handicap — if the Good To Firm ground rides faster than expected and the pace is truly strong, that burden could blunt its finishing effort in the final 100 yards.

Rogue Bullet's sim-going record of 0W1P on fast surfaces is a quiet concern — it has the lead to itself but its ability to convert that lead on Good To Firm over five furlongs is genuinely unproven despite its recent form.

Kiss And Run at 132lbs is the lightest of the hold-up pair — if the pace scenario plays into a closer's hands, the weight advantage over Lazzar (131lbs) is marginal but the cleaner recent form gives it the edge in that shape.

With only five runners and a flat course, jockey positioning from the draw and first two furlongs will be decisive — watch which of Ancient State or Sam's Xpress secures the seat directly behind Rogue Bullet, as that horse inherits the most favourable tactical position regardless of the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Drafted
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type trained by Charlie Pike with a 14-day turnaround; placed at 7f on Soft suggests the step up from 6f suits, though ten on Standard is a concern — Kieren Fox will need racing luck in a traffic-heavy finish.|

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett's eight-year-old arrives on a 17-day break with two runs for the yard in the T14 window — her natural instinct is to come from the back, but the glut of similar types means she is likely racing further forward than ideal, which tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Lowestoft
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with headgear first-time and a 17-day gap; the Standard/Lingfield form is thin (0W0P on similar going), and while Matt Crawley's runner holds a hold-up profile, being pushed out of that role by the crowded rear reduces its winning prospects materially.|

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: Has headgear (ht) and placed over 8f on Soft and 8f on Standard — Hayley Burton's six-year-old has shown she can produce a late run and the 17-day return looks straightforward; Stevie Donohoe is well-placed to ride a patient race from midfield.|

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Roger Teal has been active with 2/12 in the past 14 days; the four-year-old's true home is at the back of the field but the bunched nature of this race means she will sit in the pack rather than her preferred rear position, limiting effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Accommodation
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' three-year-old is flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern in a sprint-style finish; placed at 6f on Standard but drops back after poor recent runs, and her true hold-up role is obscured by redistribution in this crowded shape.|

runners_data.name: Blossom In The Air
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Robert Edwards with a 'fades in finish' flag and a poor record on Good to Firm adjacent going (0W0P on turf Standard); Dylan Hogan takes the ride but the lack of visible form strength makes this an unlikely beneficiary even if she secures a forward berth.|

runners_data.name: Dontwaryboutathing
runners_data.note: D Donovan's three-year-old is 64 days off the track — the longest break in the field — and has only three career runs all showing double-figure finishes or modest placings; the headgear flag (t) and the layoff together make this a significant risk in a competitive sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Mr Jeffrey
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's three-year-old has only three runs to date, all weak form (007), and the 'fades in finish' flag is a red light in a race likely decided by a furious last two furlongs; Rhys Clutterbuck will need significant improvement on anything shown so far.|

races.paceDynamic: The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions for the 7½f contest at Lingfield, and with no confirmed front-runner across the entire ten-runner field, this race is almost certain to be run at a muddled, modest gallop before dissolving into a scrambling sprint finish in the straight. Every single runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no genuine pace-maker to string the field out, and the early stages will likely see a crawl with runners bunched and jostling for position. That slow-run, compressed dynamic will compress the finish, making positional luck and a well-timed run absolutely critical — horses who can travel comfortably in the pack and produce a sharp, sustained burst will be most advantaged. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Accommodation, Rovinia, Heer's Sadie, Lowestoft, Blossom In The Air, Dontwaryboutathing and Mr Jeffrey are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield, but none of them are natural front-runners, meaning no single horse is likely to set a true pace — closers who can switch off and still quicken off a slow gallop, most likely Desert Charm and Nicely Curved, hold the strongest positional hand in this chaotic shape.

races.name: Harris & Bailey Builders Merchants 'Confined' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Savannah Smiles
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with course form and soft-ground experience; headgear unchanged, trainer Grace Harris running at a modest 2/18 over 14 days, but 12 days fresh and showed a placed effort at six furlongs on Good — her natural late-run style is ideal if Calafrio's pace is honest enough to utilise it.

runners_data.name: Orange Emperor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for James Fanshawe (6/23 T14), with a placed record on Standard and Good to Firm at this trip; Arron D'Arcy's claim helps in the weights and a hold-up profile suits the likely pace shape, with similar-going form showing a placed effort from seven runs.

runners_data.name: Calafrio
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and sole pace influence in this race; returning from a 175-day break for George Baker's yard (0/3 T14) wearing a tongue-tie, with a winning run over this course and trip on Standard — his ability to control every fraction is both his biggest asset and the caveat, as the layoff introduces fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games
runners_data.note: Held a prominent position in recent form but is a true hold-up type here; George Boughey's yard is firing at 5/34 over 14 days and the horse is quick back after just five days — its natural style sits towards the rear, which in a five-runner field with one pacesetter means it must produce a clean finishing run without much cover.

runners_data.name: My Dad Tom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon three-year-old with a deeply uninspiring recent record of consecutive sixth-place finishes; 40-day absence, hold-up style mapped to midfield due to redistribution — the form string offers little encouragement and a 0W0P record on similar going makes this a significant step-up required to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Calafrio is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over six furlongs at Lingfield. With no pressure from rivals, Liam Wright can dictate tempo entirely on his own terms, setting up a race that strongly favours hold-up horses who can track and pounce — provided the gallop is honest enough to bring them into play in the final two furlongs. The three hold-up runners — Savannah Smiles, Orange Emperor, and the redistribution pair Blindfold Games and My Dad Tom — will all be intent on closing ground late, but Calafrio's uncontested lead and ability to control the fractions means the pace may simply not be strong enough to fully suit deep closers. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent-to-tracking profile that can travel within a length or two of Calafrio before asserting; pure hold-up horses forced wide or trapped in traffic face a steeper task if the gallop is modest.

scenarios.label: A

watchPoints.text: Calafrio's 175-day absence is a major fitness risk — if he ties up or fades sharply in the final furlong, the entire pace shape collapses and the outcome becomes unpredictable for the hold-up horses tracking him.

Orange Emperor has shown placed form on Standard and Good to Firm at this trip for Fanshawe — watch whether Arron D'Arcy elects to sit closer to Calafrio than his hold-up tag suggests, potentially grabbing a crucial early position.

Blindfold Games returns just five days after its last run and is a true rear-runner in a field that will be strung out behind one front-runner — monitor whether Jack Callan finds a clear passage or gets trapped with no cover in a small field.

With only five runners and one natural pacesetter, the early stride pattern in the first furlong will be critical — any hesitation from Calafrio at the gates could prompt an unexpected rush for the lead from horses not naturally suited to it.

My Dad Tom's six consecutive finishes outside the top three on similar ground suggest it needs a significant reversal of form; Tyrese Cameron's 5lb claim provides minor weight relief but the trainer's 8/53 T14 strike rate signals a yard not at peak form.
